topic: AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer - Associate (MLA-C01) exam preparation - AWS's newest, high-demand associate certification for building, operationalizing, deploying, and maintaining ML solutions and pipelines on the AWS Cloud, centered on Amazon SageMaker
cert_name: AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer - Associate
exam_format: 65 questions (50 scored + 15 unscored), 130 minutes, passing score 720 out of 1000 (scaled), delivered online-proctored or at a Pearson VUE test center. In addition to multiple choice (one correct of four) and multiple response (two or more correct), MLA-C01 introduces newer AWS question formats: ordering, matching, and case study. MLA-C01 is the CURRENT version (general availability late 2024) and remains current in 2026. Certification is valid for 3 years.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple response clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'
audience: ML engineers, data scientists, MLOps and platform engineers, and developers who build, deploy, and operate machine learning workloads on AWS. Candidates should have roughly one year of hands-on experience with Amazon SageMaker and AWS ML/data services plus a working understanding of ML concepts. A strong technical step up from the AWS AI Practitioner (AIF-C01) and a companion to the AWS GenAI Developer (AIP-C01) and Solutions Architect Associate (SAA-C04) courses in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Data Preparation for Machine Learning (ML)
domains.notes: The largest domain. Ingest and store data: choosing storage and streaming for ML (Amazon S3, EFS, FSx for Lustre, Kinesis Data Streams/Firehose, Amazon MSK), data formats (Parquet, RecordIO, JSONL), AWS Glue and Glue Data Catalog, Athena, Lake Formation, EMR. Transform data and perform feature engineering: SageMaker Data Wrangler, SageMaker Processing, Glue/Spark, handling missing values and outliers, encoding categorical variables, scaling/normalization, binning, train/validation/test splitting, SageMaker Feature Store for reusable features, feature selection. Ensure data integrity and prepare for modeling: detecting and mitigating bias with SageMaker Clarify, class-imbalance techniques (SMOTE, resampling), data labeling with SageMaker Ground Truth, deduplication, encryption (KMS) and PII handling with Macie, data compliance. Choosing the right AWS data/prep service for a described requirement is the core skill.

domains.name: ML Model Development
domains.notes: Choose a modeling approach: SageMaker built-in algorithms (XGBoost, Linear Learner, DeepAR, etc.), SageMaker JumpStart and pre-trained/foundation models, Amazon Bedrock for GenAI, when to fine-tune vs train from scratch vs use a managed service, framing the problem (classification, regression, clustering, forecasting). Train and refine models: SageMaker training jobs, script mode and bring-your-own-container (ECR), distributed and managed spot training, automatic model tuning (AMT / hyperparameter tuning), early stopping and regularization, diagnosing and fixing overfitting vs underfitting, SageMaker Debugger. Analyze model performance: choosing and interpreting metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUC-ROC, RMSE/MAE, confusion matrix), SageMaker Experiments for tracking and comparison, model explainability and bias with Clarify, baselining and model selection trade-offs.

domains.name: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
domains.notes: Select deployment infrastructure based on requirements: SageMaker real-time endpoints, serverless inference, asynchronous inference, batch transform, multi-model and multi-container endpoints, instance-type and accelerator (GPU/Inferentia) selection, endpoint auto scaling, cost/latency/throughput trade-offs. Create and script infrastructure: infrastructure as code (CloudFormation, CDK), the SageMaker Python SDK and boto3, container images in Amazon ECR, environment consistency across dev/test/prod. Automate deployment: CI/CD for ML with SageMaker Pipelines, SageMaker Model Registry (versioning, approval), CodePipeline/CodeBuild, EventBridge triggers, Step Functions orchestration, automated retraining and promotion. Picking the most appropriate deployment and orchestration pattern for a scenario is the recurring exam skill.

domains.name: ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security
domains.notes: Monitor model performance and data quality: SageMaker Model Monitor for data-quality, model-quality, bias, and feature-attribution drift; CloudWatch metrics/alarms; A/B testing and shadow/canary deployments; detecting concept and data drift and triggering retraining. Monitor and optimize infrastructure and cost: CloudWatch and CloudTrail, right-sizing endpoints, managed spot for training, Savings Plans, scaling policies, eliminating idle capacity, cost allocation tags. Secure ML systems and resources: IAM least-privilege roles and policies for SageMaker, VPC/network isolation and PrivateLink, encryption at rest and in transit with KMS, securing data with Macie and S3 policies, secrets management, audit and compliance. Choosing the correct monitoring, cost, or security control for a described requirement is the core skill.

extra_guidance: MLA-C01 is AWS's newest and fastest-growing associate ML certification (general availability late 2024) - a high-demand, high-volume technical play as ML/MLOps hiring surges. The four domain names and weights above are AWS's official MLA-C01 exam-guide domains - use them verbatim (Data Prep 28%, Model Dev 26%, Deployment & Orchestration 22%, Monitoring/Maintenance/Security 24%). This exam is SageMaker-centric and OPERATIONAL, not a theory or math exam - the skill is choosing and wiring the right AWS/SageMaker service for a described build, deploy, or operate requirement, so practice questions MUST be scenario-based with plausible distractors and 'MOST cost-effective / LEAST operational overhead / MOST scalable' framing. Cover the classic decision pairs relentlessly: real-time vs serverless vs async vs batch inference, Data Wrangler vs Glue vs SageMaker Processing, built-in algorithm vs JumpStart vs Bedrock vs custom container, single vs multi-model endpoints, AMT vs manual tuning, Model Monitor drift types (data quality vs model quality vs bias vs feature attribution), SageMaker Pipelines vs Step Functions. NOTE the real exam also uses ordering, matching, and case-study question formats, but this course's practice tests use multiple-choice (4 options) and clearly-marked multiple-response only, per the pipeline's schema. Labs are SageMaker Studio walkthroughs and console tours at read-and-understand level (training job, endpoint deploy, Model Monitor setup, Feature Store), not deep CLI. Funnel note: this is the technical step up from AIF-C01 and pairs with AIP-C01 and SAA-C04. Final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 130-minute time-management strategy for 65 questions and guidance on multiple-response elimination. Scan the practice bank for other-vendor terms (Azure/GCP) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
